overview.professional_workflow: Understand Audience → Define Objective → Research → Build Narrative → Design Slides → Verify Evidence → Rehearse → Present → Answer Questions → Improve
core_principles: Defined purpose: every presentation aims for a specific audience decision or understanding
Audience-centric: tailored to audience knowledge, objections, time constraints, and role
Central message: unified one-sentence core takeaway supported by evidence
Evidence-based: claims backed by primary research, verified metrics, and clear citations
Visual hierarchy: intentional typography, white space, and layout guiding the eye
Chart integrity: honest baselines, accurate scales, and clear units without distortion
Presentation accessibility: high contrast, alt text, reading order, and clear labels
Speaker support: slides complement verbal explanations without turning into readable scripts
Actionable conclusion: clear next steps, decision requests, or discussion frameworks

slide_design_standards.heading: Design Slides That Help People Understand the Message.
principles: Typography: clear heading hierarchy, readable sans-serif body text, proper line height, and high contrast
Composition: intentional grid alignment, logical content grouping, and generous white space
Colour: consistent branding palette, functional colour emphasis, and contrast meeting accessibility guidelines
Visual Selection: purposeful photos, clear process diagrams, and data charts used only when they clarify meaning
Data Communication: accurate axes, zero baseline for bar charts, readable units, and transparent citations
avoid: Overcrowded bulleted paragraphs masquerading as slides
Misleading chart scales, truncated axes, or manipulated comparisons
Text-heavy screenshots that force the audience to read rather than listen

evidence_based_data_presentations.heading: Make Your Data Understandable Without Distorting the Facts.
rules: Chart Selection: bar charts for discrete categories, line charts for continuous trends, tables for exact values
Context & Sourcing: mandatory source attribution, sample timeframes, and measurement units
AI Chart Verification: rigorous human audit of AI-generated numbers, aggregations, scales, and labels
Data Slide Checklist: answers what the chart shows, where data originated, the timeframe, unit, and supported takeaway

presentation_accessibility.heading: Make Presentations Understandable to More People.
features: Sufficient colour contrast between text and background
Descriptive alternative text (alt text) for critical diagrams and charts
Logical reading order verified through software Accessibility Checkers
Describing essential visual takeaways verbally during delivery for hybrid/virtual attendees

responsible_ai_presentation_workflows.heading: Use AI to Develop Ideas. Verify Every Claim Before You Present.
responsible_ai_presentation_workflows.philosophy: Explore AI assistance for presentation outlines, writing, slide layouts and rehearsal. Learn to review the results for factual accuracy, audience suitability, visual clarity, accessibility and originality before presenting.
appropriate_uses: Brainstorming potential audience objections and FAQ questions
Structuring raw project notes into preliminary narrative outlines
Drafting concise slide headlines that communicate takeaways
Rehearsing delivery with automated pacing and filler-word feedback
mandatory_human_verification: Auditing all numeric figures, financial metrics, and chart data points
Verifying cited sources, publication dates, and industry studies
Checking image relevance, licensing permissions, and copyright
Ensuring speaker notes align with actual spoken commitments
Protecting corporate confidentiality before uploading proprietary context to AI tools

virtual_presentation_readiness.heading: Present Professionally in the Room or on the Screen.
topics: Presenter View mastery across PowerPoint and Google Slides
Clean screen-sharing hygiene: sharing specific application windows rather than cluttered desktops
Audio and microphone checks, lighting, and camera positioning for virtual meetings
Technical contingency planning: offline PDF backup, local presentation copy, and contingency audio

highlights: 5 Weeks of intensive presentation planning, business storytelling, slide design, and live delivery (40 guided hours)
Build the complete Business Presentation & Storytelling Portfolio: 8–12 slide deck, 5–7 min recorded delivery, slide redesign, planning brief, and revision log
Master business storytelling frameworks: Problem → Solution, Situation → Complication → Resolution, and Question → Analysis → Answer
Design clean, professional slides in PowerPoint or Google Slides using visual hierarchy, typography, intentional white space, and consistent grids

Deliver and review a five-to-seven-minute presentation.

deliverables.description: A 5–7-minute recorded delivery demonstrating clear verbal explanation, slide coordination, controlled pacing, purposeful pauses, and responses to at least two realistic audience questions.

deliverables.name: Component 04: Presentation Planning Brief
deliverables.description: A comprehensive planning document defining the audience profile, business objective, central message, evidence sources, narrative framework, delivery constraints, and technical backup plan.

deliverables.name: Component 05: Structured Revision Log
deliverables.description: A structured tracking register documenting mentor critique, peer review findings, implemented slide refinements, fact verification checks, and final accessibility sign-off.

faq.question: What is Presentation Skills & Business Storytelling?
faq.answer: It is a practical course covering audience analysis, storytelling, slide design, business data communication and professional presentation delivery.

faq.question: Is this only a PowerPoint course?
faq.answer: No. PowerPoint or Google Slides is used to create presentations, but the course focuses on strategy, storytelling, visual communication and delivery.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. Basic communication skills and computer literacy are recommended. Previous presentation-software experience is helpful but not mandatory.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Five weeks with 40 guided learning hours.

faq.question: What is the fee?
faq.answer: ₹5,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: What will I learn about business storytelling?
faq.answer: You will learn to create a central message, build a logical narrative, support arguments with evidence and develop a clear conclusion.

faq.question: Will I learn slide design?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes typography, colour, layout, visual hierarchy, white space, charts and accessibility.

faq.question: Will I use Microsoft PowerPoint?
faq.answer: PowerPoint is one of the primary software options. The classroom selects one main production tool while introducing transferable skills.

faq.question: Will I use Google Slides?
faq.answer: Google Slides is included as a primary software option and may be chosen for main classroom production.

faq.question: Is Canva required?
faq.answer: No. Canva is an optional supporting tool for visual design.

faq.question: Will I learn business charts?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn to select appropriate chart types, explain data clearly and avoid misleading representations.

faq.question: Will I learn how to create presentation narratives?
faq.answer: Yes. You will develop an audience-focused presentation outline and slide-by-slide storyboard.

faq.question: How many slides will my portfolio contain?
faq.answer: The main portfolio presentation must contain eight to twelve slides.

faq.question: Will I need to record a presentation?
faq.answer: The portfolio includes a five-to-seven-minute assessed presentation, with appropriate consent and approved assessment alternatives where needed.

faq.question: Will I practise audience questions?
faq.answer: Yes. You will practise answering questions, clarifying concerns and responding honestly when information is unavailable.

faq.question: Will I learn virtual presentations?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes screen sharing, presenter notes, microphone checks and contingency planning.

faq.question: What is the slide redesign exercise?
faq.answer: You will improve an ineffective slide and explain how the redesign strengthened clarity, hierarchy and accessibility.

faq.question: Will I learn presentation accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. The course introduces contrast, alt text, reading order, chart readability and accessible slide structure.

faq.question: Can AI help me create presentations?
faq.answer: Yes. AI can assist with outlines, wording, layout ideas and rehearsal, but content and data must be checked.

faq.question: Can AI-generated charts be trusted automatically?
faq.answer: No. Numbers, chart types, scales, units, data sources and conclusions must be verified.

faq.question: Is Microsoft Copilot required?
faq.answer: No. Paid Copilot functionality is optional and subject to license and product availability.

faq.question: Is this the same as Public Speaking?
faq.answer: No. This course focuses on slide-supported presentation communication. Public Speaking is a separate specialization.

faq.question: Will I learn advanced PowerPoint animations?
faq.answer: The course covers appropriate slide design and presentation controls. Advanced PowerPoint production is outside the core curriculum.

faq.question: What portfolio will I create?
faq.answer: An eight-to-twelve-slide deck, five-to-seven-minute recorded delivery, before-and-after slide redesign, planning brief and revision log.

faq.question: Does the course guarantee confident speaking?
faq.answer: The course provides structured rehearsal and feedback to develop presentation skills. Individual progress varies, and a particular confidence level cannot be guaranteed.

faq.question: Will this course guarantee business sales or investor funding?
faq.answer:
No. It develops communication and presentation skills but cannot guarantee audience decisions or commercial outcomes.
